visual_review.scope: Static exported contact sheets and comparison still, plus original run source comparison. This review does not claim uninterrupted animation viewing or an engine playtest.
visual_review.isolation_limit: No obvious neighboring body or sword fragments appear in the inspected exported contacts. Connected defects already painted into a selected source body cannot be ruled out by connected-component tests.
visual_review.identity: Silver/red hair, black/red coat, chest straps, double red forearm wraps and dark segmented greaves remain recognizable. Approval against standard_v1 remains with the user.

attack1.recommendation: Keep as a source/quality review candidate, not an approved replacement.
attack1.positive: Clear ready, drawn-back windup, forward release and recovery poses; the restored blade in pose 2 is attached to the grip and no neighboring body fragment is visible.
issues: Poses 3/4 read as a forward extension, then pose 5 turns the torso away and carries the blade backward again. Whether this reads as one forceful slash rather than a second windup needs real-speed user review.
The recovery poses 7/8 hold 14 of the 30 ticks. This may be intentional, but perceived weight and recovery length are not established by a contact sheet.
Visible blade length and angle vary between poses; perspective may explain part of it, but no validated grip/guard/tip or G3 weapon-layer contract is present.
The V6 comparison still aligns body scale and shows a recognizable common identity; it cannot establish that the new whole action meets the V6 motion and quality gate.

run.recommendation: Enough to review running pose/style and proposed rhythm as a partial-cycle candidate. Do not label it a complete accepted run loop.
run.comparison_with_c1: C2 has real second-half changes, especially poses 5 and 7; it is more than an unchanged repeated row.
issues: Poses 2/6 and 4/8 remain very close. The second half does not clearly communicate the opposite near/far-leg roles through all contact, passing and flight phases.
Eight occupied cells must not be counted as eight verified gait phases. The opposite half-cycle still needs a clear leg-role check before batch production or integration.
The upper body, free fist and sword remain comparatively rigid; the contact sheet shows leg changes and bobbing more clearly than coordinated arm/shoulder motion.

The two flight poses have visibly different ground clearances, about 19 and 26 output pixels for the marked foot. This can be intentional, but symmetry, loop seam and support-foot sliding remain unapproved.

jump_demo.recommendation: Keep as a phase/arc review candidate; the staged sequence is readable but is not runtime-approved.
jump_demo.positive: Push-off, ascent, tuck at apex, descent, contact, compression and recovery are distinct. Separate output heights 8/50/80/50/0/0/0 preserve a complete visible arc without snapping every lowest foot to ground.
issues: The 32-tick arc is represented by a few held poses and discrete height changes. Smoothness and matching engine jump physics remain unverified.
Contact to deep compression changes the marked support point substantially; actual same-foot anchoring and landing continuity require motion review.
The preparatory crouch is a separate clip and is not included in the 32-tick jump_demo. A full gameplay state sequence must explicitly connect that clip if preparation is desired.
